newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened sharply against the dollar and basket of foreign currencies in mixed, volatile trading on Monday following political unrest and the rise of the dollar against the mark, dealers said.

"Trading was very volatile today and activity was very high. The dollar rose to 3.2470 shekels because of the political tension and the rise of the dollar abroad. By midday the dollar started back falling for no evident reason," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"Investors are very confused. People were buying dollars because of the clashes but others started selling once the dollar rose," he said.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.2200 against 3.1920 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5958 shekels against 3.5679 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8905 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8848 on Friday and against the mark at 2.1093 shekels per mark against 2.0963 on Friday.
The Bank of Israel set the representative rate early on Monday due to the Jewish holiday of Succoth and will do so throughout the week.
In the afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2060 shekels.
